title: Currency review of the tasks and oracle milestones: relabel-reviewed or revise
body:
## Goal
The `tasks` and `oracle` milestones in benchmark/preparation-status.json are still `prepared-not-reviewed`. Review #179 recomputed 1,053/1,053 XML agreements of the 11 development cases (landed via #175/#176). Review #262 accepted the native design and review #297 accepted benchmark/native/readiness-case.json. Expected gain: a per-milestone verdict (relabel-reviewed or revise) so one pin script can relabel them. The next Policymaker reads the verdict and numbered findings in your report.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Turn 1: write `.session/report.md` (status wip), then update it as you go.
- [ ] tasks: by script (python3 -I, sha256), check that each development case file pinned in benchmark/preparation.json under tasks is byte-identical to the bytes reviewed by #179 (find the reviewed commit with `git log` on benchmark/dev/; use `git show <commit>:<path>`). List any changed file.
- [ ] tasks: seeded spot check (seed 302) of 10 XML slots against the original public artifacts under $LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT. Record slot id, pointer, expected, actual.
- [ ] oracle: check that every oracle pin hash matches the file on main, and that README/limitation text states that zero native executions exist (#169 not ready). The oracle label must not claim native evidence.
- [ ] Verdict per milestone: `relabel-reviewed` or `revise`, with numbered findings (file:line). Do not edit repository files.
## Verification
`python3 -I -B policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
## Context
- benchmark/preparation.json, benchmark/preparation-status.json: pins and labels.
- Review #288 (iter-0044 evidence) is the model for a currency review: byte identity + seeded spot check.
## Budget
- Do not print whole case JSON files; read only the selected slots by script. Stay under 300k input tokens.
- Do not read `.session/report.md` in Verification.

title: Find and review the restricted-store readiness record of capability #268
body:
## Goal
Capability #268 (restricted evaluation store) is approved and the owner posted capability-ready. Its readiness clause says: a loop session other than the author independently reviews the record before split work uses the store. The record is not in the repository. Expected gain: either a review verdict on the record (unblocks split allocation planning), or the exact proof that a session cannot read it (then the Policymaker asks the owner to commit a redacted record). The next Policymaker reads the verdict or the export status in your report.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Turn 1: write `.session/report.md` (status wip).
- [ ] Read `.session/exports/manifest.json`. Report the status of the `reports` export for session 268 exactly (downloaded/unavailable/expired/error/unknown) and the staged paths.
- [ ] Search the repository read-only for the record: `git grep -n -i sentinel` and `git log --all --oneline -- '*268*'`. Report hits.
- [ ] If a record is found: check that steps (a)-(e) each give identity label, operation, expected result and actual result; recompute its sha256 with python3 -I and compare with the stated value; confirm that no token value appears. Verdict accept/revise with numbered findings.
- [ ] If no record is found: report `record-unavailable` with the evidence above and stop. Do not guess its content.
- [ ] Do not edit repository files. Do not try to access the private repository.
## Verification
`python3 -I -B policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
## Context
- Readiness text: .session/loop-state.json of the Policymaker, owner request #268.
- benchmark/resources-proposal.md Row 1; benchmark/split/README.md.
## Budget
- At most 20 tool calls. Do not open case JSON, results JSON, sources.json or lineage.json.
